paragraphs.title: The Holiness of Zion and God’s Love for Jerusalem

answers: In the holy mountains
In the deserts of Egypt
In the valleys of Babylon
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “His foundation is in the holy mountains.”
easy.q: Where is God’s foundation said to be?

answers: The gates of Zion
The armies of Israel
The rivers of Egypt
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “The LORD loveth the gates of Zion.”

answers: Glorious things
Secret things
Terrible things
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God.”
easy.q: What is spoken of the city of God?

answers: He loves Zion more than all of them
He loves them all equally
He does not love Zion
medium.explanation: The LORD loves the gates of Zion “more than all the dwellings of Jacob.”
medium.q: How does the LORD’s love for Zion compare with His love for Jacob’s dwellings?

answers: Honourable and magnificent
Hidden and uncertain
Sorrowful and weak
medium.explanation: “Glorious” describes things that are splendid, honourable, and worthy of praise.
medium.q: What does the word “glorious” mean in “Glorious things are spoken of thee”?

answers: They move from holy mountains, to Zion’s special place, to praise of the city
They move from war, to judgment, to exile
They move from Egypt, to Babylon, to Ethiopia
medium.explanation: The verses progress from the holy mountains to God’s love for Zion and then to glorious words about the city.
medium.q: How do the first three verses develop their main idea?

answers: Zion has a uniquely favored position before the LORD
Zion is outside the people of God
Jacob’s dwellings no longer exist
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes Zion’s special status in the LORD’s affection.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from comparing Zion with all the dwellings of Jacob?

answers: Both express the city’s honor and distinction
Both describe the city’s destruction
Both refer to foreign nations
challenge.explanation: Calling Zion the city of God reinforces the glorious description given to it.
challenge.q: How does the title “city of God” relate to the glorious things spoken of Zion?

answers: The sacred character of Zion
The wealth of Zion
The distance of Zion
challenge.explanation: The reference to the holy mountains highlights Zion’s holiness.
challenge.q: What does the connection between Zion and the holy mountains emphasize?

paragraphs.title: Zion as a Distinguished Place of Birth

answers: Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia
Egypt, Rome, Greece, and Spain
Samaria, Damascus, Hebron, and Gaza
easy.explanation: Verse 4 names Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia.
easy.q: Which places are mentioned in connection with being known or having someone born there?

answers: This and that man was born in her
No man was born in her
Only one king was born in her
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “This and that man was born in her.”
easy.q: What is said about the person born in Zion?

answers: The highest himself
The kings of the earth
The nations
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “the highest himself shall establish her.”

answers: A notable person may be mentioned from other lands, but every person born in Zion is specially recognized
The nations are never mentioned, but Zion is forgotten
All the nations and Zion are treated as exactly the same
medium.explanation: The passage mentions people associated with other lands but especially declares that each person born in Zion is recognized.
medium.q: What is the main contrast between the nations and Zion in these verses?

answers: One person and another person, or each individual
Two kings only
A person whose identity is unknown
medium.explanation: The wording indicates individual people generally, emphasizing each one born in Zion.
medium.q: What does the expression “this and that man” suggest?

answers: The LORD both establishes Zion and records those associated with being born there
The nations establish Zion and the LORD ignores them
Counting the people removes Zion’s importance
medium.explanation: The verses attribute both Zion’s establishment and the recognition of its people to the LORD.
medium.q: What connection is shown between establishing Zion and counting the people?

answers: Birth in Zion is acknowledged and recorded
The place of birth has no importance
The LORD does not know Zion’s people
challenge.explanation: The LORD counts and records the person born there, showing that the birth is significant.
challenge.q: What does the LORD’s counting of the people indicate?

answers: They mention many lands while emphasizing those recognized in relation to Zion
They limit belonging to one foreign nation
They deny any connection between Zion and other peoples
challenge.explanation: The passage names several lands and then highlights the special standing of those born in Zion.
challenge.q: How do verses 4–6 broaden the idea of belonging to Zion?

answers: In Zion, distinction is extended to every person born there
Only one person can be born in Zion
No people live in the other lands
challenge.explanation: The wording contrasts an individual mention elsewhere with the broad recognition of every person born in Zion.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the contrast between an individual associated with another land and “this and that man” born in Zion?

paragraphs.title: Praise, Song, and Longing for Jerusalem

answers: The singers and the players on instruments
The kings and the soldiers
The priests and the judges
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there.”
easy.q: Who is mentioned as being there?

answers: As participants in joyful praise
As silent mourners
As warriors preparing for battle
easy.explanation: Their presence with singing and instruments conveys joyful praise.
easy.q: How are the singers and instrumental players presented?

answers: In thee
In Babylon
In the holy mountains only
easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “all my springs are in thee.”
easy.q: Where are all the speaker’s springs?

answers: Joyful praise
Fearful silence
Anger and division
medium.explanation: Singers and instrumental players together create an image of joyful worship and praise.
medium.q: What do singing and playing instruments together express?

answers: Sources of life, desire, and blessing
Only literal streams of water
Military strongholds
medium.explanation: “Springs” is figurative language for the sources of the speaker’s life, desire, and blessing.
medium.q: What does “springs” most likely represent in “all my springs are in thee”?

answers: It expresses joyful devotion and directs the speaker’s deepest sources toward Zion
It changes the subject to foreign nations
It rejects the holiness of Zion
medium.explanation: The music and the statement about all the springs being in Zion complete the psalm’s praise of the city.
medium.q: How does the final verse relate to the earlier praise of Zion?

answers: The speaker’s deepest sources of life and longing are centered in Zion
Zion contains only physical wells
The singers have no connection with Zion
challenge.explanation: The metaphor presents Zion as the source and focus of the speaker’s deepest desires and vitality.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “all my springs are in thee”?

answers: It concludes the description of Zion’s greatness with celebration and devotion
It turns entirely to a description of foreign lands
It denies that Zion is special
challenge.explanation: The final verse answers the earlier praise with musical celebration and personal longing.
challenge.q: How does verse 7 complete the ideas of the psalm?

answers: The speaker’s devotion and longing are wholly directed toward Zion
Only a small part of the speaker’s desire is directed toward Zion
The speaker’s desires are divided among many places
challenge.explanation: “All” stresses the completeness and totality of the speaker’s attachment to Zion.
challenge.q: What does the word “all” emphasize in “all my springs are in thee”?
